name: cli-init-refuse-existing
body: `kalide init` refuses (clear message, non-zero exit, nothing written) if `slides/`, `assets/` or `kalide.yaml` already exists — with or without a path argument. An existing `templates/` blocks init ONLY when no path argument is given. When a path argument is given, a pre-existing local `templates/` is exempt from the check: init proceeds, writes the deck referencing the external path, and the local `templates/` is ignored (never deleted, never overwritten). Other files (e.g. `.git`, or a legacy `eypres.yaml`, which is not recognised) do not block. There is no `--force` flag.
